four_layer_diagnosis.integration: coupled but inert (inert by STARVED UPSTREAM): the event reaches the relief block once per event (C5), but the VALENCE_LIKING write is a silent no-op (ResidueField.update_valence returns at _nearest_active_center None; residue/field.py:944-946, 973-974) and the beta release branch is never entered because no commitment ever forms in this harness. Missing links: (i) no active residue center -- the loop never calls agent.update_residue; (ii) no commitment driver -- beta_gate_bistable=False and no commit/closure coupling, 0 elevated ticks. Neither is a latch defect.

learning_extracted: The latch works at its output: the comparator now emits about one relief-completion event per detected norm-descent (shadow burst) on the real agent loop -- note a 'descent' is a >=30-tick-gap shadow burst, NOT a damage event (seed 45: 89 onsets-with-rise -> 18 bursts -> 15 events), as the driver pre-registered (docstring lines 29-35).

Cross-arm trajectories are bit-identical in all 3 seeds (steps, episode lengths, norm range, injections): flipping the latch changed the event count 21x and changed nothing the agent did. Expected once neither arm has any event side effect -- it measures THIS harness, not the latch's reach in general (step 7b C7).

Integration gap discovered (inert by STARVED UPSTREAM): in the 517/1110 harness shape the relief event reaches NO native consumer -- VALENCE_LIKING writes are silent no-ops without an active residue center, and no commitment ever forms (beta_gate_bistable=False; 0/3,000 elevated ticks in the red-team probe), so there is nothing to release. The superseded 517c 'writes' metric and 1110's C5 both measured CALLS, not effects.

Instrument lesson (recording/measurement gap, forward-only): any future SD-050/MECH-302/MECH-304 test must count consumer EFFECTS (inner rbf valence writes, LIKING mass delta at the target center, beta releases with beta elevated, store prototype updates), not relief-block calls.

Design note surfaced (not adjudicated): the relief tag lands on the nearest ACTIVE harm-residue center with no valence bounding by default; under the pre-latch train that would have been ~9-24 x +1.0 LIKING writes per descent onto a harm center -- the latch matters most exactly at the half 1110 did not exercise.

routing_options.A: SCOPE-AND-FOLD: governance applies the scoped latch validation (refractory entry -> validated for event emission only), SD-050 stays candidate, and the consumer half is folded into SD-050's existing CONFIRMING-test gate (agent-produced descent + BOTH reuse sites per fire), which is itself gated on the registration-only action-contingent-relief-provider (priority 4, design doc owed). No new experiment now. Cost: the consumer-half question waits on an unscheduled env design.
routing_options.B: SCOPE-AND-PROBE (recommended): as A, PLUS /queue-experiment one new-number diagnostic that exercises the unexercised native consumers with latch ON vs OFF on a bed that HAS both prerequisites -- natural candidate is V3-EXQ-916a's bed (ree-v3/experiments/v3_exq_916a_relief_safety_fishtank_showcase.py: comparator ON :378, config.heartbeat.beta_gate_bistable=True :389, agent.update_residue in-loop :688/:874; 60 relief fires in its 2026-08-11 run, but seed-1 gave 0 -> seed-risk for the precondition). 1110's own bed CANNOT serve the beta half: it forms no commitment at any tick, so a precondition of >=N beta-elevated relief ticks would fail deterministically there; if 1110's bed is kept, B must add an explicit commitment lever (bistable latch + commit driver, or a scripted beta_gate.elevate() arm) or drop the beta half. DVs: inner VALENCE_LIKING writes per event and LIKING mass delta at the written center; beta releases at events with beta elevated (plus the elevated-tick denominator, which 1110 did not record); optional arm SD-051 prototype updates per descent. Precondition per seed: >=1 active residue center AND >=N beta-elevated relief ticks, else substrate_not_ready. D2 on the consumer edges, decoupled from action-contingency (which stays SD-050's CONFIRMING test). Not a duplicate: 916a scored no consumer effects and no queue item or driver tests them (red-team F10). Owner: /queue-experiment, chipped by governance after ratification.

step7b_dispositions.C7: ACTED ON, not dismissed -- and it is informative. shadow_fires (and steps, episode lengths, norm_min/max, max_window_drop, curriculum_injections) are bit-identical across ARM_LATCH_OFF and ARM_LATCH_ON in every seed (recomputed from arm_results). The shadow is an instrument on the agent's own norm stream, so identity is expected only if trajectories never diverged -- and they did not, despite the driver's warning that they MAY diverge after the first event. Reading: the latch changed the event flag (46 vs 989 fires) but changed NOTHING downstream of it in this loop -- a direct measurement that the event is behaviourally inert here (no beta release, no landed tag). It strengthens the scoping; it does not undermine C1/C2 (which are within-ON-arm latched-vs-shadow comparisons, not cross-arm).
